title: Geometric nearby-cycle finiteness and proper/smooth exchange
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and algebraically closed field $k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and the trait $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$, its strict henselization, and its chosen geometric generic point from [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be separated finite-type $D$-schemes, with special fibres $\mathcal X_0,\mathcal Y_0$ and geometric generic fibres $\mathcal X_{\bar\eta},\mathcal Y_{\bar\eta}$. On small etale sites, define $R\Psi_{\mathcal X}K=i_{\mathcal X}^*Rj_{\mathcal X*}K$ as in that specialization datum. Bounded constructibility is [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and finite Tor amplitude is the existence of a finite interval $[a,b]$ outside which $K\otimes_A^LF$ has zero cohomology for every module sheaf $F$ in degree zero [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-kun-tor-amplitude].

The functor $R\Psi_{\mathcal X}$ takes every bounded constructible etale complex on $\mathcal X_{\bar\eta}$ to a bounded constructible complex on $\mathcal X_0$, and takes those of finite Tor amplitude to those of finite Tor amplitude. It is exact triangulated, computed on functorial derived models; cones of its natural exchange transformations can consequently be taken on those models compatibly with triangles. For a $D$-morphism $h:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ (proper as in [def-weil-proper-morphism], smooth as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]), the canonical exchanges are isomorphisms for every bounded constructible etale complex $K$ on $\mathcal X_{\bar\eta}$ and every bounded constructible etale complex $L$ on $\mathcal Y_{\bar\eta}$:
$$R\Psi_{\mathcal Y}Rh_{\bar\eta*}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{0*}R\Psi_{\mathcal X}K\quad(h\text{ proper}),$$
$$h_0^*R\Psi_{\mathcal Y}L\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Psi_{\mathcal X}h_{\bar\eta}^*L\quad(h\text{ smooth}).$$
They are the maps induced by the inverse/direct-image adjunctions in $i^*Rj_*$, and respect composition, identities and the nearby-cycle unit $i^*H\to R\Psi(j^*H)$. Their adjoint mates, including exceptional exchanges for the constructible compact-support adjunctions, have the same composition and unit/counit compatibilities.

source.place: §1.3.1(e) (nearby-cycle bounded constructible finite-Tor domain), §1.3.2(b)--(c) (exchanges and adjoint mates), and §3.2.1 / Remark 3.2.5 (use on bounded constructible complexes)

proof.text: Work after the chosen strict henselization; write $X=X^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $j:X_{\bar\eta}\to X$ and $i:X_0\to X$. The coefficient ring is finite, killed by a power of $\ell$ invertible on the trait. The geometric generic map $j$ is affine (an algebraic field extension composed with the principal generic open immersion), hence qcqs; it is not being treated as an open immersion or a finite-type morphism. Exactness of $i^*$ and right-derived exactness of $Rj_*$ make $i^*Rj_*$ an exact triangulated functor on the ambient derived categories, in particular on bounded-below inputs. All subsequent module cohomology computations may be forgotten to abelian sheaves and recovered: the canonical bounded-below comparison is an isomorphism for every scheme morphism.

Fix a geometric point $x$ of $X_0$. The strict-henselization stalk formula identifies $(R\Psi K)_x$ with $R\Gamma(X_{(x)}\times_{D^{\mathrm{sh}}}\bar\eta,K)$. Express $X_{(x)}$ as the inverse limit of affine etale neighborhoods $U$ of $x$ in $X$; use a small cofinal system, with affine transition maps. After base change to $\bar\eta$, all $U_{\bar\eta}$ are affine schemes of finite type over the separably closed geometric generic field $\bar K$. The fixed coefficient complex is pulled back from $T=X_{\bar\eta}$, exactly as required in the derived continuity theorem. Thus in each degree the stalk cohomology is $\varinjlim_U H^r(U_{\bar\eta},K)$. The same computation applies to $K\otimes_A^L\underline M$ whenever that tensor is bounded below. In step 10 this holds for every module $M$, including infinite ones, because the finite-Tor hypothesis puts this tensor in $D^{[a,b]}$. No bounded-below assertion for that tensor is made for a general bounded $K$.

source.place: §1.3.1(e), stalk computation expanded using ordinary etale continuity

proof.text: Assume $X_{\bar\eta}$ nonempty and choose a finite integer $d\geq\dim X_{\bar\eta}$. An etale map preserves local dimensions, so $\dim U_{\bar\eta}\leq d$. Apply the relative torsion direct-image dimension bound to $U_{\bar\eta}\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar K$: it is qc and locally finite type, its target is over the separably closed field $\bar K$, and $A$ is torsion. Hence its cohomology on every module sheaf vanishes above $2d$. Step 2 then gives $R^q\Psi F=0$ for $q>2d$ for every sheaf $F$. For a complex with cohomology in $[c,e]$, finite induction over its truncation triangles, using step 1, gives nearby-cycle cohomology in $[c,e+2d]$. Vanishing at every stalk gives vanishing of the sheaf. If the geometric generic fibre is empty, $j_*=0$ and all these conclusions hold with the zero complex without choosing its dimension.

source.place: §1.3.1(e), finite cohomological bound; see Stacks dimension bound cited by the referenced node

proof.text: Let $K_0=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$ and let $\bar K$ be the field of the chosen geometric generic point, an algebraic closure of $K_0$ (if it is a separable closure, everything below holds with $K^s=\bar K$ and $\pi$ the identity). Let $K^s\subseteq\bar K$ be the separable algebraic closure of $K_0$ in $\bar K$: it is a separable closure of $K_0$, and $\bar K/K^s$ is purely inseparable. Put $\pi:X_{\bar K}\to X_{K^s}$ and $j^s:X_{K^s}\to X$, so $j=j^s\pi$. A base change of $\pi$ along a morphism $Y\to X_{K^s}$ is $Y\times_{K^s}\bar K\to Y$, a homeomorphism for every $K^s$-scheme $Y$; so $\pi$ is a universal homeomorphism. Topological invariance makes $\pi^{-1}$ and $\pi_*$ quasi-inverse equivalences of etale sheaf categories, compatible with inverse images; the constant rings correspond, so the same holds for $A$-module sheaves. Hence $\pi_*$ is exact and $R\pi_*=\pi_*$. For a module sheaf $F$ on $X_{\bar K}$ put $F^s=\pi_*F$, so $\pi^{-1}F^s\simeq F$; pushforward composition gives $Rj_*F\simeq Rj^s_*R\pi_*F=Rj^s_*F^s$, hence $i^*R^qj_*F\simeq i^*R^qj^s_*F^s$ for every $q$.

source.place: Tag 03SI (topological invariance of the etale site, universal homeomorphisms); Illusie (2021) §1.1 uses a separable closure of eta, which this step compares with the chosen algebraically closed geometric generic point

proof.text: Let $F$ be constructible on $X_{\bar K}$, with strata $T_k$ taken with their reduced structures $Z_k$ and immersions $\iota_k$, as the definition allows. The homeomorphism $\pi$ of qcqs schemes preserves quasi-compact opens, hence constructible and locally closed subsets, so the sets $\pi(T_k)$ form a finite partition of $X_{K^s}$ into locally closed constructible subsets. Give $\pi(T_k)$ its reduced structure $Z'_k$, with immersion $\iota'_k$. The base change $Z'_k\times_{X_{K^s}}X_{\bar K}\to X_{\bar K}$ is an immersion with image $\pi^{-1}\pi(T_k)=T_k$, so $Z_k$ is its reduction; thus $\rho_k:Z_k\to Z'_k$ is a surjective closed immersion followed by a base change of $\pi$, a composite of universal homeomorphisms, hence a universal homeomorphism, and $\iota'_k\rho_k=\pi\iota_k$. So $\rho_k^{-1}\iota_k'^{-1}F^s\simeq\iota_k^{-1}\pi^{-1}F^s\simeq\iota_k^{-1}F$ is finite locally constant: choose an etale cover $\{U_i\to Z_k\}$ and finite $A$-modules $M_i$ with restrictions $\underline{M_i}$. By the site equivalence for $\rho_k$, $U_i\simeq U'_i\times_{Z'_k}Z_k$ for an etale cover $\{U'_i\to Z'_k\}$; the projection $U_i\to U'_i$ is a universal homeomorphism, whose inverse-image equivalence carries both $(\iota_k'^{-1}F^s)|_{U'_i}$ and $\underline{M_i}$ to $\underline{M_i}$. Hence $(\iota_k'^{-1}F^s)|_{U'_i}\simeq\underline{M_i}$, and $F^s$ is constructible on $X_{K^s}$.

source.place: Tag 03SI (topological invariance), with the stratum definition of constructibility (Tag 03RW region); written out by the maintainer reader

proof.text: Let $L$ range over the finite subextensions of $K^s/K_0$; each is finite separable, since $K^s/K_0$ is separable algebraic. The schemes $X_L$ are qcqs, the transition maps are affine, and their inverse limit is $X_{K^s}$: on an affine chart this is the identity $B\otimes_{K_0}K^s=\varinjlim_L(B\otimes_{K_0}L)$, as $K^s$ is the union of these $L$. The finite subextensions form a small directed set (the compositum contains any two). Constructible-module limit descent therefore gives, for the constructible $F^s$ of step 5, a finite separable $L/K_0$ and a constructible $F'$ on $X_L$ with $F'_{K^s}\simeq F^s$. Let $v:X_L\to X_{K_0}$. It is finite etale: finiteness is obtained by tensoring a finite $K_0$-basis of $L$ on each affine chart, and etaleness follows from the finite separable field-extension theorem and its base-change stability. The target is Noetherian because it is finite type over the field $K_0$, so the finite morphism $v$ is of finite presentation. Thus $G=v_*F'$ is constructible and $Rv_*F'=G$, by finite pushforward finiteness over the field $K_0$.

source.place: Tags 09YU (lemma-category-is-colimit)(3), 095R (lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible); descent and finite direct image on the arithmetic generic fibre

proof.text: Base change $v$ along $X_{K^s}\to X_{K_0}$, writing $P=X_L\times_{X_{K_0}}X_{K^s}$, $w:P\to X_{K^s}$, $b:P\to X_L$, and $H=b^*F'$. The inclusion $L\subset K^s$ gives a section $s:X_{K^s}\to P$ of $w$. Both $v$ and $w$ are finite, hence proper (in particular $w$ is separated), and $w$ is etale. The section theorem identifies $s(X_{K^s})$ as an open and closed subscheme of $P$. Proper base change for $v$ identifies $G_{K^s}$ with $w_*H$ (higher direct images vanish by the finite-image theorem; its target is finite type over $K^s$ and Noetherian, so $w$ is finite presentation). For every etale $V\to X_{K^s}$, the two disjoint opens over $s(X_{K^s})$ and its complement give $H(P\times V)=H(V\times s(X_{K^s}))\times H(V\times(P\setminus s(X_{K^s})))$. Restriction to the first factor and inclusion with zero on the second commute with restrictions and are $A$-linear. By the inverse-image/restriction theorem for the etale map $s$, its first factor is the sections of $s^*H=F'_{K^s}\simeq F^s$; thus these are sheaf maps $F^s\xrightarrow{u}G_{K^s}\xrightarrow{r}F^s$ with $ru=1$. No trace divided by $[L:K_0]$ is used.

source.place: Finite proper base change and the clopen-section decomposition, applied to the geometric generic base change of v; elementary sectionwise sheaf-product calculation

proof.text: The ring $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring: it is strictly henselian local, and since $k[t]_{(t)}$ (the localization of a principal ideal domain at a nonzero prime) is a discrete valuation ring, so is its strict henselization. Its fraction field is $K_0$, $\operatorname{Spec}K^s$ is a separable closure of its generic point, and its closed fibre is $X_0$ with the map $i$ of the specialization datum. $X$ is separated and finite type over $D^{\mathrm{sh}}$, and $A$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, which is invertible in $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ since $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k$. Apply the standard sheaf nearby-cycle theorem to the constructible sheaf $G$ on the generic fibre $X_{K_0}$: $C_q=i^*R^qj^s_*(G_{K^s})$ is constructible for every $q$ and eventually zero. Apply the additive functor $i^*R^qj^s_*$ to $u,r$ of step 7: the maps $U_q,R_q$ satisfy $R_qU_q=1$. The projector $e_q=U_qR_q$ is an endomorphism of the constructible sheaf $C_q$, and its kernel $\ker(1-e_q)$ is constructible by Serre closure. The maps $U_q,R_q$ identify that kernel with $i^*R^qj^s_*F^s$, which is $i^*R^qj_*F$ by step 4. This proves constructibility of the nearby cycles of the arbitrary geometric-generic sheaf $F$. The uniform bound for all sheaves remains the independent bound of step 3.

source.place: Luc Illusie, Grothendieck and vanishing cycles, Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse 30 (2021), §1.1, formula (1.2), and §1.2, last paragraph, printed pp. 85–86: specialize to a sheaf in degree zero; finite constant coefficient-ring form by retaining its action. Read online; local archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\bar\eta},A)$. It is obtained by finitely many truncation triangles from its constructible cohomology sheaves shifted by their degrees. Steps 4–8 and the bound of step 3 give bounded constructible nearby cycles of each of those shifted sheaves. Apply the exact functor of step 1 to the truncation triangles. At each induction stage the cohomology long exact sequence expresses each new cohomology sheaf as an extension of a cokernel by a kernel of morphisms between constructible sheaves. Closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions gives constructibility. The common interval of step 3 gives boundedness. This proves the assertion for all bounded constructible complexes, without assuming finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: §1.3.1(e), passing from sheaves to bounded complexes by truncation triangles

proof.text:
Now suppose $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. For every affine neighborhood $U$ of step 2 and every $A$-module $M$, scalar projection gives
$R\Gamma(U_{\bar\eta},K)\otimes_A^LM\simeq R\Gamma(U_{\bar\eta},K\otimes_A^L\underline M)$.
Its hypotheses hold: $U_{\bar\eta}$ is qcqs and finite torsion cohomological dimension follows from clause (2) of [lem-kun-0f10], since it is finite type over the separably closed field; the uniform A-cohomology bound is separately step 3. Inverse image is monoidal, so the right-hand input has cohomology in $[a,b]$; step 3 gives output cohomology in $[a,b+2d]$. Choose bounded-below resolution models for the restriction diagram of step 2, with their natural comparison maps. The resolution-naturality lemma computes the derived restriction maps on these models. Their colimit maps to the limit-space cohomology model, and step 2 makes this a quasi-isomorphism. Filtered colimits commute with cohomology: for the kernel assertion a represented element whose image becomes zero is already zero at a common later index, and cokernels commute with colimits by their universal property. Tensor commutes with that colimit as well: compute $-\otimes_A^LM$ by a fixed bounded-above free resolution of the degree-zero module $M$, whose tensor total complex uses direct sums, and take the filtered colimit term by term. Thus $(R\Psi K)_x\otimes_A^LM$ has cohomology only in $[a,b+2d]$.

source.place: §1.3.1(e), finite Tor assertion expanded via scalar projection on affine neighborhoods

proof.text: For an arbitrary module sheaf $G$ on $X_0$, exact monoidal stalk pullback identifies $(R\Psi K\otimes_A^LG)_x$ with $(R\Psi K)_x\otimes_A^LG_x$. Apply step 10 with the possibly infinite module $M=G_x$. Stalks commute with cohomology and detect zero sheaves, so $R\Psi K\otimes_A^LG$ has no cohomology outside $[a,b+2d]$, uniformly for every $G$. This is precisely finite Tor amplitude; no assumption that the cohomology modules of $K$ are flat is used.

source.place: §1.3.1(e), conversion of scalar bounds at stalks to the full module-sheaf Tor condition

proof.text:
Suppose $h:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ proper, and base change it to the strict henselian trait. Properness persists under this base change. The equality $j_Yh_{\bar\eta}=h j_X$ and the canonical composition comparisons give
$i_Y^*Rj_{Y*}Rh_{\bar\eta*}K\simeq i_Y^*Rh_*Rj_{X*}K$.
Apply proper base change for the torsion ring $A$ to $h$ and the special immersion $i_Y$, with input $Rj_{X*}K$. That input need not be bounded constructible on the total trait; the cited theorem is valid on the unbounded module category and hence applies. It gives
$i_Y^*Rh_*Rj_{X*}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{0*}i_X^*Rj_{X*}K$.
The composite is the required proper exchange. The generic proper pushforward is bounded constructible by finite-type-over-a-field constructibility, applied over the field $\bar K$ (not to the total trait); thus the left side is within the just-established nearby-cycle domain.

source.place: §1.3.2(b)--(c), proper exchange written through ordinary proper base change

proof.text:
Suppose $h$ smooth. In the generic-fibre Cartesian square with bottom arrow $j_Y:Y_{\bar\eta}\to Y$ and vertical arrows $h$ and $h_{\bar\eta}$, smooth base change gives
$h^*Rj_{Y*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{X*}h_{\bar\eta}^*L$.
Here $h$ is smooth and $j_Y$ is qcqs by step 1; the finite coefficient exponent is invertible on $Y$. The theorem only requires $L$ bounded constructible on $Y_{\bar\eta}$ and does not require $Rj_{Y*}L$ constructible on $Y$. Pull back by the exact functor $i_X^*$ and identify $i_X^*h^*=h_0^*i_Y^*$ to obtain the required smooth exchange. Pullback of a finite constructible stratification, and of its finite locally constant restrictions, shows that $h_{\bar\eta}^*L$ is bounded constructible, so this too is within the nearby-cycle domain.

source.place: §1.3.2(b)--(c), smooth exchange through the generic-fibre square

proof.text: Use the general abelian-category clause of the filtered-operation lift theorem on small etale module categories. Exact inverse images lift termwise; $Rj_*$ and the adjunction exchanges lift with unchanged forgetful maps. Compute bounded-below objects by injective resolutions. The resolution-naturality lemma identifies their augmentation squares before cohomology and supplies cone resolutions (finite sums of injectives remain injective), so the following calculation computes the derived exchanges. For $alpha:P^\bullet\to Q^\bullet$, use $\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha)^r=Q^r\oplus P^{r+1}$ with differential $(q,p)\mapsto(dq+\alpha p,-dp)$. For a commuting square $A\xrightarrow{a}B$, $C\xrightarrow{b}D$ with vertical maps $u:A\to C$, $v:B\to D$, the two iterated cones have terms $D^r\oplus C^{r+1}\oplus B^{r+1}\oplus A^{r+2}$ and $D^r\oplus B^{r+1}\oplus C^{r+1}\oplus A^{r+2}$. The map $(d,c,b_0,a_0)\mapsto(d,b_0,c,-a_0)$ intertwines their differentials: the two mixed entries are $u a_0$ and $-a a_0$, whose signs both reverse. Hence interchanging the cone directions gives an isomorphism. Applying this to an exchange on a cone triangle gives the triangle of defect cones, compatibly with its maps. This uses the specified resolution and filtered lifts, rather than inferring a functorial cone from triangulated exactness alone.

source.place: §3.2.1 and Remark 3.2.5, defect-cone use; filtered model enhancement from the cited operation-lift theorem

proof.text: The exchanges in steps 12--13 were made from the actual inverse/direct adjunction units and counits and the canonical composition comparisons. For two composable morphisms substitute those formulas: mate-pasting along the nonadjoint sides identifies the two-square composite with the mate of the outer square; pasting along the adjunctions inserts exactly the unit $R_1\eta_2L_1\circ\eta_1$ and counit $\varepsilon_2\circ L_2\varepsilon_1R_2$. This proves composition compatibility; the identity clause gives identity compatibility. The nearby unit is $i^*\eta_j(H):i^*H\to i^*Rj_*j^*H$. Naturality of $\eta_j$ and the triangle identities give the same pasted-square identity with this unit inserted.

source.place: §1.3.2(b), adjoint exchanges and their compatibility with the specialization unit

proof.text:
For compact supports, use the actual transformation $B_h:Rh_{0!}R\Psi_X\to R\Psi_YRh_{\bar\eta!}$: its formula is the inverse compact-support base change along $i_Y$, followed by the map $i_Y^*Rh_!Rj_{X*}\to i_Y^*Rj_{Y*}Rh_{\bar\eta!}$ adjoint to
$j_Y^*Rh_!Rj_{X*}\simeq Rh_{\bar\eta!}j_X^*Rj_{X*}\xrightarrow{Rh_{\bar\eta!}\varepsilon_{j_X}}Rh_{\bar\eta!}$.
This is the construction specified in the deformation definition. All these schemes are qcqs, h is separated finite type, and Nagata supplies the compactifications, including those of two composable maps and their composite. The compact-support base-change theorem supplies its naturality and horizontal/vertical pasting on bounded-below etale inputs. Substituting the displayed counit formula into a composite $hg$, that pasting and naturality of the counit give $B_{hg}=(B_hRg_{\bar\eta!})\circ(Rh_{0!}B_g)$ after the compact-support composition identifications. Identity base changes and the adjunction triangle identities give the identity and nearby-unit equations. Take its exceptional mate only on the constructible domains where the fibre adjunctions are supplied. The mate-pasting and changing-adjunction equations carry these equations to the exceptional exchanges, with the same unit/counit compatibilities. No exceptional functor on all complexes over the total trait is introduced.

source.place: §1.3.2(b), construction of compact-support exchange and its exceptional mate

The separate Tor, exchange and model arguments are retained.

split_report.summary: Repair of return a88651d2e8: withdrew the finite-stage domination lemma rather than repushing it. Replaced it with the explicitly named standard nearby-cycle constructibility/vanishing theorem for a constructible sheaf on the arithmetic generic fibre, read online in Illusie (2021) §1.2. Existing 09YU descent, finite pushforward and proper base change give a split inclusion of an arbitrary geometric-generic sheaf into an arithmetic sheaf after geometric pullback; the projector kernel gives constructibility. The source-attribution/archive question is escalated in report.md for HUMAN.md. Retained and reread the independent bound, Tor-amplitude, exchange, cone and mate arguments. No statement change, Lean work or push. Maintainer-reader FIX (2026-10-17): the new input is stated for a constructible sheaf on the arithmetic generic fibre, exactly as Illusie (2021) p.86 states it; new steps 4-5 pass from the chosen algebraically closed geometric generic field to the separable closure by topological invariance before the separable descent; step 8 cites the strict-henselization DVR lemma for the trait hypothesis.
